title: Movies & Cinema
text: Films that left a deep mark on me — reflecting on themes of theoretical physics, cosmic exploration, time, and human tenacity.

entries.title: Interstellar
entries.subtitle: Christopher Nolan (2014)
entries.thought: The visualization of gravitational time dilation near Gargantua and Kip Thorne's real general relativity calculations made physics feel profoundly emotional. The docking sequence scored by Hans Zimmer's pipe organ remains an unmatched pinnacle of tension and human grit.

entries.title: Oppenheimer
entries.subtitle: Christopher Nolan (2023)
entries.thought: A visceral portrait of theoretical physics, quantum uncertainty, and the catastrophic ethical weight of scientific breakthrough. The sound design during the Trinity test silence gave me literal chills in the theater.

entries.title: Blade Runner 2049
entries.subtitle: Denis Villeneuve (2017)
entries.thought: Roger Deakins' cinematography and the desolate brutalist architecture created an unforgettable atmosphere. A quiet, contemplative study on consciousness, artificial intelligence, and what makes human emotion authentic.

entries.title: Arrival
entries.subtitle: Denis Villeneuve (2016)
entries.thought: Fascinating exploration of the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis and nonlinear time perception. The idea that learning a language can rewire your temporal consciousness was deeply thought-provoking.

title: Books & Literature
text: Books across physics, computational mechanics, mathematics, and hard science fiction that fundamentally reshaped how I think.

entries.title: The Feynman Lectures on Physics
entries.subtitle: Richard P. Feynman
entries.thought: Feynman's intuition for classical mechanics and electromagnetism taught me to visualize physical principles before touching a differential equation. It is the purest benchmark for conceptual clarity in engineering.

entries.title: Finite Element Procedures
entries.subtitle: Klaus-Jürgen Bathe
entries.thought: The definitive foundation for nonlinear solid mechanics and continuum element formulations. Walking through continuum kinematics and arc-length solver algorithms gave me the exact rigor to write numerical solvers.

entries.title: Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid
entries.subtitle: Douglas Hofstadter
entries.thought: A masterpiece connecting formal logic, recursive self-reference, Bach's canons, and cognitive emergence. It bridged formal mathematics with aesthetics in a way that stayed with me forever.

entries.title: The Three-Body Problem Trilogy
entries.subtitle: Liu Cixin
entries.thought: The cosmic sociology and dimensional collapse concepts made this the most mind-bending hard science fiction I have ever read. The Dark Forest axiom gave me a genuine sense of cosmic awe and dread.

title: Music & Soundtracks
text: Albums and film scores that power late-night coding sessions and mathematical derivations.

entries.title: Interstellar Original Motion Picture Soundtrack
entries.subtitle: Hans Zimmer (2014)
entries.thought: Recorded on the 1926 Harrison & Harrison organ at Temple Church. The massive chord progressions in 'Cornfield Chase' and 'No Time for Caution' provide unmatched focus and emotional momentum.

entries.title: In a Time Lapse
entries.subtitle: Ludovico Einaudi (2013)
entries.thought: Minimalist piano interwoven with soaring string arrangements. 'Experience' is my ultimate focus anthem when debugging complex finite element routines.

entries.title: Awake
entries.subtitle: Tycho (2014)
entries.thought: Warm analog synths, crisp live drums, and sun-drenched melodies. The ideal rhythm for deep software architecture work without vocal distraction.
